name: PT Laman Mining
summary: PT Laman Mining holds a bauxite mining concession in West Kalimantan. Nusantara Atlas satellite data, as reported by The Jakarta Post, show at least 640 ha of burn scar inside it between January and July 2026. A spokesperson quoted in the same article, named there as being for 'PT Lamang Mining', said the fires were outside the company's mining permit area and came from nearby community plantations and other concessions. This profile does not establish who lit any fire.

source.publisher: Asia News Network (republishing The Jakarta Post)

burnedHa.method: Burned area inside the concession for January to July 2026, as measured by Nusantara Atlas and reported by The Jakarta Post (published 11 September 2026). We did not measure it ourselves and have not seen the underlying Nusantara Atlas dataset. The figure is given as 'at least 640 ha' and the article lists the company fourth among the ten concessions with the largest burned area.

evidence.summary: Nusantara Atlas satellite data, as reported by The Jakarta Post, show at least 640 ha burned inside the concession between January and July 2026. This is satellite detection of burned area. It does not show how the fires began. The company disputes that the burn scars are inside its permit area (see response).

source.title: Local, foreign firms own largest burned concessions in Indonesia's Kalimantan
source.publisher: Asia News Network (republishing The Jakarta Post)

response.summary: The Jakarta Post quotes spokesperson Prayudi Valentinus, named in the article as speaking for 'PT Lamang Mining', as saying the company's mining business permit (IUP) lies outside the area monitored by Nusantara Atlas. He said the company reported fires in March but that they were not inside its IUP and came from nearby community plantations and other concessions. The article spells the company name differently from its own list ('Laman'), and we have treated the two as the same company because the statement concerns a mining permit in the same story.
